image.alt: A Syngonium Red Plum Allusion in a white embossed pot, its arrowhead leaves olive green flushed with plum and veined in red

light.label: Bright indirect light
light.note: Tolerates medium light, but the plum fades back towards olive

landscape_use.note: Frost-free zones only; keep out of direct sun

snap: A compact arrowhead Syngonium whose olive-green leaves are flushed plum and veined in red. Unlike its relatives it does not run — it branches from the base and holds a low mound, which makes it the one to put on a desk. Toxic to cats and dogs if chewed.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: The species grows wild in the forests of Central and South America, where it scrambles and climbs. This one belongs to the Allusion group, a set of cultivars selected for the opposite habit: compact, self-branching plants that stay put. It is sold as Plum Allusion and as Red Plum Allusion — the same plant either way.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Water when the top inch of the mix has dried, and never leave the pot standing in water. Light is what decides how it looks: bright indirect brings up the plum flush and the red veining, while a dim corner returns flat olive leaves with the colour drained out. Direct sun scorches it.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: It does not vine. An ordinary Syngonium runs once it settles in, and keeping it tidy means pinching it back or giving it a pole; this one branches from the base instead and stays a dense low mound at roughly a foot across. That is the reason to choose it over the others on a desk or a narrow shelf, where a trailing plant becomes a nuisance. The colour is the second reason: plum laid over olive, with every vein picked out in red.
